newsitem.title: USA: White House sweats out O.J. verdict.
newsitem.headline: White House sweats out O.J. verdict.

text.p: The O.J. Simpson civil trial verdict could not have come at a worse time for President Bill Clinton as he prepared to give his State of the Union speech on Tuesday night.
Asked if Clinton would delay his speech until the verdict was announced, White House spokesman Mike McCurry replied sharply: "Absolutely not."

"We're fulfilling a constitutional obligation and the courts are governed by the Constitution," McCurry said, implying that Clinton and the Santa Monica court where the Simpson trial took place were both going about their business.

The White House clearly feared that the TV networks would ignore Clinton's speech in favour of the more dramatic Simpson verdict. But McCurry said "absolutely not" when asked if the White House had asked the court to delay announcing the verdict until after Clinton spoke.
